b01-absorb: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air for photosynthesis.
b02-clouds: Condensation forms clouds: water vapour cools high in the sky and condensation forms clouds.
b03-newton: Isaac Newton described gravity as a universal attraction between masses.
b04-bees-dance: Bees communicate the location of flowers by performing a waggle dance inside the hive.
b05-magma: Magma becomes lava when it reaches the surface.
b06-books-count: Members can borrow up to ten books.
b07-oxygen: Plants release oxygen into the air during photosynthesis.
b08-evaporation: Heat from the sun causes evaporation from oceans, lakes, and rivers.
b09-tide: The gravity of the moon pulls on ocean water and raises a bulge that causes high tide.
b10-pollen: Bees, butterflies, and wind carry pollen from flower to flower.
b11-light-seeds: Wind carries light seeds with wings or fine hairs across fields.
b12-epicentre: The place on the surface above where the earthquake slip starts is called the epicentre.
b13-photovoltaic: Photovoltaic cells release electrons when sunlight strikes them.
b14-turbine-blades: Wind spins the blades of a wind turbine.
b15-hydro-gates: Hydro stations raise or lower output quickly by opening or closing gates that control the water flow.
b16-close-time: The Northlight library closes at nine in the evening on weekdays.
b17-storytime: Storytime for young children happens on Tuesday mornings in the childrens room and lasts forty minutes.
b18-navigate: Birds navigate using the sun, the stars, and the magnetic field of the earth.
b19-salmon-eggs: Salmon lay their eggs in gravel beds in their home stream.
b20-thunder: Thunder is the sound the heated air makes after lightning, a giant spark of electricity.
b21-seasons-tilt: The northern half of the earth tilts toward the sun, because the axis of the earth is tilted as the earth travels around the sun.
b22-valleys: Rivers carry stones and soil downstream as they shape valleys.
b23-loan-weeks: Members can borrow books for three weeks.
b24-bees-collect: Honey bees collect nectar and pollen from flowers to feed their colony.
p01-condensation: Water vapour cools high in the sky and condensation forms clouds.
p02-molten: Molten rock stored underground is called magma, and it becomes lava when it reaches the surface.
p05-storytelling: Storytime for young children happens on Tuesday mornings in the childrens room.
p06-byproduct: Plants release oxygen into the air while they make food by photosynthesis.
